errorCodes.meaning: Per grant, in `results[].code`: the embedded proof's `proofPurpose` is not `authentication`.

Per grant, in `results[].code`: the embedded Data Integrity proof does not verify — a bad signature, a verification method not controlled by the statement's `issuer`, or one not in the issuer's current `authentication` relationship.
Per grant, in `results[].code`: the member DID could not be resolved now, so the grant could not be checked.
Per grant, in `results[].code`: the statement's `audience` is not this mediator's DID.
Per grant, in `results[].code`: the statement's `principal` equals its `issuer`.
Per grant, in `results[].code`: the statement's `iat` is more than 60 seconds in the mediator's future.
Per grant, in `results[].code`: the statement's `exp` has passed.
Per grant, in `results[].code`: `exp − iat` exceeds the mediator's maximum grant lifetime (`maxGrantLifetimeSeconds`).
Per grant, in `results[].code`: the signed scope is empty. An empty scope is refused, never read as 'all'.
Per grant, in `results[].code`: the member DID has no account at this mediator, or it is blocked.
Per grant, in `results[].code`: the signed scope exceeds the member DID's own access-control capabilities.
Per grant, in `results[].code`: the statement's `epoch` is not the member DID's current epoch. The outcome carries `currentEpoch`; the member re-signs under it.

Per grant, in `results[].code`: the statement's `iat` is not strictly later than the principal's replay floor for this member, or than the `iat` of the grant it would replace — a revoked, replaced or superseded statement submitted again. The outcome carries `replayFloorAt`; the member re-signs with a later `iat`.
Per grant, in `results[].code`: the statement's `grantId` is already on the member DID's record.
Per grant, in `results[].code`: storing the grant would exceed the active grants allowed on the member DID.
Per grant, in `results[].code`: storing the grant would exceed the grants allowed per principal.
Per grant, in `results[].code`: the member DID's record changed under concurrent writes too many times for the grant to be committed. Nothing was stored; resubmit the same statement.

Ext.description: Vendor-namespaced extension object per SPEC.md §4.5.1. Each immediate key MUST be a reverse-DNS namespace; structure under each namespace is opaque to the framework.
Ext.title: Ext

GrantId.description: A grant's identifier, chosen by the member DID's signer and carried in its grant statement; a UUID is RECOMMENDED. A mediator refuses a grant whose identifier is already on the member DID's record.
GrantId.title: GrantId

GrantOutcome.description: The outcome for one submitted grant.

attachedNow.description: Present exactly when `status` is `stored`: whether the member was attached at once to a connection the principal holds.

code.description: Present exactly when `status` is `refused`: the first check the grant failed, in the order the specification lists them.

currentEpoch.description: Present exactly when `code` is `messaging/mux/grant:epochMismatch`: the member DID's current epoch, under which the member re-signs.

grantId.description: The grant's identifier, from its statement.

principal.description: The principal DID, from the statement.

replacedGrantId.description: Present when this grant replaced an earlier grant for the same member and principal, in whatever state that grant was. Replacing raises the principal's replay floor, so the replaced statement can never be stored again.

replayFloorAt.description: Present exactly when `code` is `messaging/mux/grant:replayed`: the instant a replacement grant's `iat` must be strictly later than — the principal's replay floor for this member, or the `iat` of the grant it would replace, whichever is later.

GrantOutcome.title: GrantOutcome

GrantStatement.description: A member DID's standing statement that the named principal may carry its traffic at this mediator, on any connection, until `exp`, within `scope`, under the member's current `epoch`. Signed by the member with an embedded Data Integrity proof whose purpose is `authentication`, and stored verbatim by the mediator as the only evidence of the delegation.

audience.description: The mediator's DID. A statement names exactly one mediator and is refused by every other.

epoch.description: The member DID's current epoch at the mediator. Only messaging/mux/revoke-all advances it.

exp.description: JWT NumericDate (RFC 7519 §2): when the statement stops being accepted. REQUIRED; MUST be after `iat` and in the future.

iat.description: JWT NumericDate (RFC 7519 §2), whole seconds since 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z UTC: when the statement was signed. MUST NOT be more than 60 seconds in the mediator's future.

issuer.description: The member DID: the signer, and the DID the statement concerns.

principal.description: The principal DID that may carry the member's traffic. MUST differ from `issuer`.

type.description: Always `muxGrant`; names the statement kind, so a statement of one kind is never accepted as another.

GrantStatement.title: GrantStatement

MuxDataIntegrityProof.description: The W3C Data Integrity proof embedded in a mux statement, made by the member DID: the format and verifier Trust Tasks already use for document proofs (SPEC §4.7). The proof covers the whole statement except `proof` itself, as the cryptosuite defines. Closed: a member Data Integrity defines but this list omits is refused.

created.description: OPTIONAL: when the proof was made, as Data Integrity defines it. Covered by the proof; the statement's own `iat` is what the mediator checks.

cryptosuite.description: The W3C Data Integrity EdDSA cryptosuite used.

proofPurpose.description: MUST be `authentication`. Any other value is refused with `messaging/mux:proofPurposeInvalid` — a proof made for another relationship (an `assertionMethod` credential signature, say) is never accepted as control of the DID.

verificationMethod.description: The DID URL of the verification method that signed. MUST be controlled by the statement's `issuer` and listed in that DID's current `authentication` relationship.

MuxDataIntegrityProof.title: MuxDataIntegrityProof

MuxDid.description: A DID, carried verbatim and compared by exact string equality. Unlike the messaging family's `Vid`, never a hash: the mediator resolves it to verify a statement signed by it. For a member DID reached over TSP, the TSP VID is the DID itself.
MuxDid.title: MuxDid

MuxScopeValue.description: One capability a member DID extends to a principal's connection. `receive`: live delivery of the member's inbound messages on the connection. `pickup`: message-pickup status and delivery requests naming the member as `recipient_did`, and inclusion in a raw-TSP inbox drain. `delete`: deleting the member's stored messages, including delete-on-ack and delete-on-send; a member without `delete` keeps its messages in its inbox until something holding `delete` collects them. `send`: the mediator accepts on this connection frames whose sender is the member DID — the frame is still signed or authcrypted with the member's own keys; the scope only lets the mediator accept it on this socket.
MuxScopeValue.title: MuxScopeValue

Response.description: The success response to a messaging/mux/grant request: one outcome per submitted grant, in request order. Carried in a Trust Task document whose type is https://trusttasks.org/spec/messaging/mux/grant/0.1#response.
Response.title: Messaging — Mux Grant — response payload

StatementScope.description: The scope a member DID signs into a statement: a JSON array of MuxScopeValue, compared as a set — order is not significant and a repeated value collapses. It MUST NOT be empty; an empty signed scope is refused with the task's `emptyScope` code, never read as "all". Unlike MuxScope, emptiness is not a schema failure here, so that the refusal is reported per statement rather than failing the whole batch.
StatementScope.title: StatementScope

schema.description: Store or replace grants: each a grant statement in which a member DID, with an embedded Data Integrity proof, delegates to a principal the carrying of its messages, under the member's current epoch and an explicit scope and expiry. The outer document members are owned by the framework — SPEC §6.3.

grants.description: The grant statements to store; the member DID is each statement's `issuer`. Each is checked and answered on its own; the batch is never all-or-nothing.

schema.title: Messaging — Mux Grant — payload
